top_story.headline: Immigration agency plans no-bid deal with Procentrix to link its A-File records to the immigration court and citizenship systems
top_story.dek: The value is redacted, and the justification was posted October 16, after the September 30 start date it lists for the 12-month modification.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement intends to modify its existing Records and Information Management Unit task order with Procentrix LLC on a sole-source basis. The 12-month modification buys Alien-File (A-File) records modernization and integration support. According to the justification, the work would connect the Office of the Principal Legal Advisor's PLAnet litigation case management system with the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services STACKS digital A-File repository through Immigration and Customs Enforcement's data mesh and API gateway. The dollar value is redacted in the posted document.

The agency cites the 'logical follow-on' exception under FAR 16.507-6(b)(3), meaning the order is sole-sourced for economy and efficiency because it follows an order already placed under the contract. The underlying contract is the Scalable Ways to Implement Flexible Tasks (SWIFT) Collaborative Services indefinite-delivery contract, and the task order is 70CTD024FR0000094. The modification covers September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027, concurrent with Option Period 2, and the document says it does not extend the task order's existing period of performance. The notice was posted October 16, after that start date.

The justification leans on incumbency. It says Procentrix 'has current operational responsibility for the accepted baseline' of the records environment that must be modified, and it warns of 'unmanageable division of accountability between multiple vendors that could compromise system and records integrity.' It also cites Executive Order 14243, which directs agencies to reduce information silos and facilitate authorized sharing of unclassified records. According to the extraction, Procentrix has a federal contract on record in USAspending going back to 2010.

sections.headline: Veterans Affairs buys a new nurse call system for its Dayton hospital without competition after two alarm failures
paragraphs: There were 22 new justifications, 11 of them posted under other notice types such as Special Notice. Nine repeats from earlier editions were left out. The Top Story and four bridge or extension items (listed under Extensions) are not repeated here; the remaining 17 are below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs buys a new nurse call system for its Dayton hospital without competition after two alarm failures
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The Dayton VA Medical Center wants a Rauland Responder 5 Nurse Call System, integrated with Vocera, for parts of Buildings 330 and 320. The justification says the old Responder 4 system has reached end of life and replacement parts are no longer available. It describes two 2026 incidents: on May 6 the Vocera interface did not route calls to the assigned staff, and on June 3 at about 2:30 a.m. a veteran fell and disconnected the call-light cord, but 'no alarm occurred.' The agency says GMP is the only authorized Vocera dealer that can provide the complete integrated solution. The agency posted this as a Special Notice, and the value is redacted.

blocks.title: Interior Department buys 6,000 cubic yards of wildfire mulch from a local logging company without competition
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Interior, Bureau of Land Management
blocks.text: The mulch is meant to stabilize slopes above Heise, Idaho, burned in the Big Rock Fire. The agency says erosion and debris-flow risk is escalating and snow is coming. Its market research found that Forest Concepts no longer makes the product, Mountain Pine Manufacturing quoted $680,000, and Wilcox Logging quoted $60,000 because the mulch is a byproduct of its logging next to the burn area. The sole-source choice is therefore also the cheapest quote on file. The notice was posted as a Special Notice.

blocks.title: DARPA gives Ginkgo Bioworks and the University of Michigan follow-on ice-control research without competition
meta: Ginkgo Bioworks, Inc.; University of Michigan
up to $5 million combined for all Phase III awards
only one company can do it
blocks.text: Phase III of the Ice Control for Cold Environments program covers formulation, testing and scale-up of ice-modulating molecules, with 12 to 18 months per award. The justification says the Phase II performers hold proprietary data and validated testbeds, that a new contractor would need 12 to 18 months to replicate them, and that government partners are planning demonstrations for winter 2026-2027 timed to Arctic exercises. It records prior government investment of $5.207 million in Ginkgo and $8.356 million in the University of Michigan. DARPA filed a separate justification for each performer.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: State Department keeps 652 foreign service families in temporary housing on a no-bid bridge after its extension options and contract vehicles ran out
paragraphs: Four new bridge contracts or extensions were posted October 16: the State Department lodging program, a Health and Human Services repatriation contract, and two Defense Logistics Agency food contracts for the same vendor.

blocks.title: State Department keeps three temporary lodging providers for 652 foreign service families without competition as the recompete drags on
meta: Madison Hospitality Services, LLC; Interim Homes, Inc.; Executive Apartment Inc.
urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: The bridge contracts last three months with a three-month option and replace task orders 19AQMM24F0667, 19AQMM24F0674 and 19AQMM24F0670. The justification says the extension-of-services clause was already exercised in full under each order and the underlying indefinite-delivery contracts have expired. A recompete has closed and proposals are under review, but award is not expected before the orders lapse. The program houses personnel training at the George P. Shultz National Foreign Affairs Training Center in Arlington, Virginia, plus medevac cases and other Washington-area needs. Without the bridge the families face 'extreme risk of eviction.'

blocks.title: Health and Human Services extends Deloitte's repatriation support contract six months without competition
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Health and Human Services, Administration for Children and Families
blocks.text: Task order 75ACF121F80033 ran from September 30, 2021 to September 29, 2026 with all four option periods exercised. The modification pushes it to March 29, 2027 with no further options. The agency says transition steps such as onboarding and training cannot be done in time, and any lapse would hurt support for an estimated 600 to 1,000 returning U.S. citizens a year. The extra work includes partner engagements at ports of entry and finance and reimbursement training for state, local and nongovernmental partners, prompted by recent emergency repatriations.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency extends its Europe and Africa ship food contract with EFS Ebrex for 425 days without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The bridge runs October 15, 2026 through December 14, 2027 and covers prime-vendor food supply to ships in Northern Europe, Southern Europe and North Africa, and West Africa. The current contract, awarded October 15, 2021, expires October 14, 2026. Its maximum was raised from $140 million to $385 million in November 2024 after a noncompetitive increase. The agency blames 'external factors' that delayed the competitive follow-on and says the new awardee will need up to 180 days to ramp up. The guaranteed minimum is $3.3 million.

items: Defense Logistics Agency extends EFS Ebrex's Western Africa food contract with an estimated $700,000 bridge without competition. The justification cites the July 2023 Niger military takeover, which disrupted supply routes and forced airlifts. (SPE30027D4113)

paragraphs: There were 87 new solicitations; 82 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Amendments to previously listed notices (the Coast Guard's Response Boat Small III and a New York courthouse elevator job, among others) are omitted unless they changed substance.

meta: General Services Administration, Federal Acquisition Service
blocks.text: The October 16 notice says the September 10, 2026 decision in BEAT-LDI JV LLC et al. v. The United States (Case No. 25-cv-00082) requires General Services Administration to act before it proceeds with awards. Amendment 0013 in the Polaris submission portal contains the required action, which applies only to offerors that bid by October 7, 2022 and extended their offers through March 31, 2025. sections.headline: Army signed a $128.9 million Patriot missile production modification and a $23.7 million Patriot adjustment, both just published
paragraphs: USAspending showed 45 new awards of $2 million or more, 31 of them Defense Department awards just published after the 90-day hold, plus 5 large modifications and 6 cuts. Eleven of these actions are featured below. The 45 routine actions are listed, each linked, in 'USAspending: Every Other New Award' at the end of the edition. Defense items below were signed July 17 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay.

blocks.text: Notable awards

Belt Built CFM Joint Venture, LLC won $5,860,944 from the Department of the Army for a firm-fixed-price construction project at the Naval Research Laboratory in Washington, D.C. The classification is repair or alteration of office buildings. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Black & Veatch Special Projects Corp. received $13,813,157 from the Army, through the Kansas City District of the Army Corps of Engineers, for architect and engineering work. The firm will prepare a design-bid-build request for proposals for a Homeland Defense Over the Horizon Radar project with land acquisition. The description says it is a sole source. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Windsor Group LLC won $5,498,082 from Washington Headquarters Services for subject matter experts in 'specialized and strategic support services' for the Office of Strategic Capital. The description gives no further detail on the work. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)

Continuity Global Solutions LLC received $3,766,735 from the Department of the Air Force for construction security surveillance services supporting secure construction projects. Its performance work statement refers to project B3267 and contract FA520526D007. It was signed July 17 and published this week. (award)
Patriot missile production

Lockheed Martin Corporation had two Army actions on Patriot Advanced Capability-3 missile production, both signed July 17 and published this week. One is a supplemental agreement for work within scope (modification P00079) adding $128,933,590. The other is a definitized letter contract (modification PZ0137) with a net change of −$23,711,189. The description does not say work was reduced, so the negative figure may reflect a pricing settlement rather than a program cut. (+$128.9M modification, −$23.7M modification)
